methods.definitionFocus: Each possible sample of size n has the same chance of selection.

procedure.text: Create a complete sampling frame of all eligible units.
Assign each unit a different number from 1 to N.
Generate random integers from 1 to N using a suitable generator.
Ignore repeated numbers and continue until n different numbers have been obtained.
Select the units corresponding to those n numbers.

conditionalProcedure.condition: If using random digit tables or a source that can yield numbers outside 1 to N
conditionalProcedure.text: Ignore numbers outside the valid range as well as repeats.

methods.workedExample: For 15 out of 120 pupils, number pupils 1-120 and generate random integers from 1-120, ignoring repeats until 15 distinct numbers are obtained.
methods.warning: Do not automatically add 'ignore out-of-range numbers' when the generator is constrained to 1,...,N; that detail applies to digit tables or an unconstrained source.

methods.definitionFocus: Regular intervals from an ordered list with a random start.

procedure.text: List or number all N eligible units in a sampling frame.
For an exact integer ratio, calculate the interval k = N/n.
Select a random starting position from 1 to k.
Select that position and then every kth unit until n units have been chosen.

conditionalProcedure.condition: When N/n is not an integer
conditionalProcedure.text: Use a random starting point followed by a suitable systematic pattern that gives the requested number; there is no single universal 'round N/n' rule.

methods.workedExample: For 20 from 100, k = 5. A random start of 2 yields 2, 7, 12, ..., 97.
methods.warning: An ordering with a periodic pattern can distort a systematic sample. A random start does not remove every ordering problem.

methods.definitionFocus: Create mutually exclusive strata, then select randomly within each.

procedure.text: Divide the population into mutually exclusive strata using a relevant characteristic.
For proportional allocation, calculate each share as (size of stratum / population size) × total sample size; ensure the final whole-number allocations sum to n.
Use a sampling frame to randomly select the required number of different units from each stratum; ignore repeats within a stratum.
Combine the selected units from all strata into one sample.

methods.workedExample: A school has 300 Year 12 and 200 Year 13 pupils. For a proportional sample of 50, randomly select 30 from Year 12 and 20 from Year 13.
methods.warning: Stratified sampling is not the same as quota sampling: selection within each stratum must be random.

methods.definitionFocus: Fill predefined group quotas without random selection of individuals.

procedure.text: Choose relevant population characteristics and divide the population into suitable groups.
Set the target number to recruit from each group, often reflecting population proportions.
Approach available eligible people without a random selection procedure, adding them to their appropriate group.
Stop recruiting for a group when its quota is full; continue until all group targets have been filled.

methods.workedExample: To survey 50 shoppers with a 60:40 split, interview eligible available shoppers until 30 from one group and 20 from the other have responded.
methods.warning: A proportional quota does not guarantee the full sample is representative, because selection within groups is non-random.

methods.definitionFocus: Recruit available eligible people at the time and place of investigation.

procedure.text: Identify the eligible population or required criteria.
Approach people who are readily available at the chosen place and time.
Collect responses from available, eligible volunteers until the required sample size is reached.

methods.workedExample: Ask the first 20 eligible shoppers willing to respond at one supermarket entrance on Monday morning.
methods.warning: The time and location may systematically exclude relevant members of the population.
